clue.text: Levy on fatty food?

parts.note: a corporation is an old jokey word for a big belly, so a tax on what fattens one is the business tax on companies

explanation.surface: A government considers a tax to discourage greasy, fattening meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is old British slang for a paunch; the question mark flags the pun that turns a tax on companies into a tax on stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the levy charged on company profits, read whimsically as a duty on one's belly.

clue.text: Lord Chancellor has written terribly drily on case law

indicators.note: the following words are set down badly, in a jumbled order, so their letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior judge's legal writing on precedent is criticised as clumsy and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Wolsey, Henry VIII's chief minister, held the office of Lord Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor churchman Thomas Wolsey served Henry VIII as Lord Chancellor of England.

clue.text: Financial factors creating a forest, perhaps

parts.note: the letters of the two short words '... among themselves, spell out the phrase 'a forest'

explanation.surface: An economist wonders which money matters lead to a woodland being planted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put the letters of RATESOF through an exchange and they yield A FOREST, which the clue gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency conversion values are key financial variables in trade and investment.

clue.text: Moose oil refined for a song

indicators.note: oil that is refined is processed and altered, so the letters of these two words are reworked into new order

explanation.surface: Oil rendered from an elk is purified and sold cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous Neapolitan ballad, a staple of tenors.

clue.text: Semites, some Muslims Barack upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the run is read from the bottom up
only some letters of the following words are used, a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Some Muslim people were displeased with President Obama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes SBARA from the end of Muslims and start of Barack; 'upset' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic speakers are a Semitic people, alongside Hebrews and others.

clue.text: Forerunner of Skype lacking volume, it's said

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter is removed from the device

parts.note: a videophone, a telephone with a camera and screen, came before internet calling services

explanation.surface: An early video-calling gadget is described as having no sound control.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the brief 'it's said': an ideophone is a word spoken to evoke a sense impression vividly, such as 'zigzag'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideophone is a vivid sound-symbolic word, something uttered in speech.

clue.text: First-class return from one African country to another

indicators.note: taking from means removing, so the reversed letters come out of the country's name

parts.note: Nigeria is a large West African state

indicators.note: return means going back, so the letters for top quality are read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone returns first-class on a flight between two African nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-class' is A1, written AI; 'return' makes IA, which leaves the end of NIGERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a separate landlocked West African nation next to Nigeria.

clue.text: Braced for conflict?

parts.note: ready for war, with a pun on orthodontic braces fixed to the teeth

explanation.surface: Soldiers steel themselves before a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braced' suggests orthodontic braces on teeth, and the idiom means heavily equipped with weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fully armed and equipped for combat.

clue.text: Former president smuggled trifle inside vehicle

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the two pieces sit in the middle of the president's name

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president
to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled gives ran
to trifle or sport with someone is to toy with them

explanation.surface: An ex-president sneaks a dessert into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'trifle' the British pudding, but it is a verb meaning to toy or play; 'smuggled' is the past tense of running contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: A car transporter is a lorry that carries many cars, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Logical basis for 15 getting left in charge

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the island and letter go into the fee

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee
the answer to clue 15, the Hebridean island

explanation.surface: An argument's reasoning is credited to some person who has been left in control.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification for something.

clue.text: School qualification of the third highest grade

parts.note: a gam is a school, or pod, of whales
an MA, Master of Arts, is a degree qualification

explanation.surface: A pupil gains a diploma at only a middling mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a place of learning here but a group of whales, a gam.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third Greek letter, used as the third grade in some marking systems.

clue.text: Semites in diaspora, apparently

indicators.note: a diaspora is a scattering of people, so the letters of the word are dispersed into new order

explanation.surface: Jewish people living abroad seem to be the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are hedging phrases meaning seemingly, on the face of it.

clue.text: A one point stone

parts.note: a as in 'a day' means per
the Roman numeral I is one
a dot is a point

explanation.surface: A single point on a scoreboard is awarded for a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means each, as in 'ten pounds a head', giving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of olivine.

clue.text: Ridiculous clot in FIFA is a cause of severe distress

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurdly out of order, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish idiot inside football's governing body causes great suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: An affliction is a source of pain or suffering, such as an illness or misfortune.

clue.text: Colourless hydrocarbon created in experiment

indicators.note: an experiment tries things out in new combinations, so the letters are recombined

explanation.surface: A chemist makes a clear organic compound in the laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Tridecane is an alkane with thirteen carbon atoms, a colourless liquid.

clue.text: Hebridean location of newspaper proprietor, it might be said

indicators.note: it might be said tells us the island's name is how a phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: the owner of the i, a British newspaper, is an 'i owner'

explanation.surface: The Scottish island where a press baron lives is being mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily newspaper, a sister title of the Independent; its owner is an 'i owner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island of the Inner Hebrides off Mull, famed for its abbey.

clue.text: Book about Tarka for example discovered under library

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed animal comes under, below, the shortened library
about means turned round, so the animal is written backwards

parts.note: Tarka is the otter in Henry Williamson's novel Tarka the Otter

explanation.surface: A book about a famous otter turns up in a library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is the text of an opera or musical, not a volume on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the book, the words, of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Not Hard Times in particular

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the multiplication sign goes into the other word

parts.note: a way is a respect or particular, as in 'in some ways'
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A Dickens novel, Hard Times, is singled out for comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard Times' looks like the Dickens title but splits into the definition and the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Something waxy is soft and yielding like wax, so not firm.

clue.text: Of course they're not main components

definitions.text: Of course they're not main components

parts.words: Of course they're not main components
parts.note: parts of a meal course that are not the main item, such as vegetables served on the side

explanation.surface: Someone states the obvious about secondary parts of a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally' but means 'belonging to a meal course'.
explanation.definitionFit: Accompaniments served alongside the main plate are minor elements of a meal.

clue.text: Operetta composer consuming very last of cheese and port

indicators.note: consuming means eating, taking inside, so the composer's name swallows a letter

parts.note: Franz Lehár composed the operetta The Merry Widow

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A composer of light opera eats cheese and drinks port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine paired with cheese, but it is the harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French seaport at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Horrible to find a hole in material

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the ring shape goes into the adjective

parts.note: vile means horrible
the letter O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: It is dreadful to discover a tear in some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Voile is a thin, semi-transparent fabric of cotton or silk.

clue.text: Good seafaring name for sailor back in Ohio perhaps

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed seaman goes into the jumbled state
perhaps hints that the state name is only one possibility, so its letters may be in another order
back means returning, so the word for a seaman is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor returning to an American state is given a fine nautical name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes RAT from TAR, which goes into HOIO, the scramble of OHIO signalled by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson, Britain's great admiral, is the classic seafaring forename.

clue.text: Listened to senior teacher about educational fundamental

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the teacher's title goes round the letter

parts.note: a head is a head teacher, the senior teacher of a school
R stands for one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A head teacher hears a talk on basic schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so one R is an educational basic.
explanation.definitionFit: To have heard something is to have listened to it.

clue.text: Dissatisfaction with regular samples of Lennon music

indicators.note: regular samples are letters taken at even intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up with hearing the same bits of John Lennon's songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and discontent from lack of interest.

clue.text: How one might describe actors having a bit of a kip outside flat

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the coin's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: the kip is the currency of Laos, and the at is a hundredth of a kip
actors are men with a part, 'part men'

explanation.surface: Actors are described as napping briefly outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kip' looks like British slang for a nap, but is the Laotian currency, divided into at; AT goes round PART MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a self-contained flat.

clue.text: Superior title

parts.note: the head of a convent, a Mother Superior, is addressed by this formal style

explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' seems an adjective, but it is the Mother Superior of a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the honorific form of address given to the head of a nunnery.
